concepts.why: The patient's left fronto-orbital swelling, progressive vision deterioration, and expansive lytic bony lesion involving the orbital walls are consistent with fibrous dysplasia of the orbit.
The patient's left fronto-orbital swelling, proptosis, and heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof are consistent with an orbital meningioma.
The patient's expansive lytic bony lesion involving the orbital walls could be consistent with an orbital osteoma.

aliases: Meningioma of the optic nerve sheath
concepts.why: The patient's progressive vision deterioration and globe displacement are consistent with an optic nerve sheath meningioma.
The patient's left fronto-orbital swelling and heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof could be consistent with an orbital lymphoma.
The patient's left fronto-orbital swelling and heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof could be consistent with an orbital metastasis.
The patient's progressive vision deterioration, globe displacement, and expansive lytic bony lesion involving the sphenoid wing are consistent with a sphenoid wing meningioma.
The patient's left fronto-orbital swelling and heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof could be consistent with an orbital schwannoma.

rationales.F01: The long duration of the swelling suggests a slow-growing process, which is consistent with fibrous dysplasia of the orbit.
rationales.F02: Progressive deterioration of vision is a common symptom of optic nerve sheath meningioma and sphenoid wing meningioma.
rationales.F04: The recent increase in proptosis suggests an expanding mass, which is consistent with several orbital tumors.
rationales.F07: The heterogeneous enhancing mass in the left orbital roof is highly suggestive of a meningioma or other tumor.
rationales.F08: The expansive lytic bony lesion involving the superior and lateral walls of the orbit is highly suggestive of fibrous dysplasia of the orbit or sphenoid wing meningioma.
